### AWS Orders Two Million More Nvidia GPUs for 2027–28

- Canonical: https://mmlong818.github.io/ai-pulse/articles/aws-orders-two-million-nvidia-gpus.html
- Chinese: https://mmlong818.github.io/ai-pulse/zh/articles/aws-orders-two-million-nvidia-gpus.html
- Source timestamp: 2026-08-26T23:47:00.000Z
- Site timestamp: 2026-08-27T11:00:03.973Z
- Tags: Industry

Amazon will deploy two million additional Blackwell Ultra and Rubin-generation GPUs while extending Nvidia technology across AWS and robotics.

## A hyperscale commitment

Amazon Web Services and Nvidia announced that AWS plans to deploy two million additional Nvidia GPUs across its global infrastructure during 2027 and 2028. The order covers Blackwell Ultra, Rubin and Rubin Ultra accelerators and follows an earlier commitment, announced five months ago, to deploy more than one million Nvidia GPUs. Financial terms were not disclosed, but an order of this scale implies spending worth tens of billions of dollars.

The agreement extends well beyond accelerator purchases. AWS plans to incorporate Nvidia’s Vera CPUs and networking technology into future systems, while offering Nvidia’s Nemotron open models through Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker. Amazon will also use Nvidia’s Omniverse simulation platform, Cosmos world models, Isaac robotics software and Jetson edge hardware across warehouse and physical-AI work, including robot training, synthetic-data generation and route optimization.

## Cooperation alongside competition

The expansion is striking because Amazon has invested heavily in reducing its reliance on Nvidia. Its Trainium accelerators compete for AI training and inference workloads, while its Graviton CPU business has reached a reported $25 billion annualized revenue run rate. AWS also has large infrastructure commitments from customers including Anthropic and OpenAI, giving it a strong incentive to develop lower-cost in-house silicon.

Yet customer demand still requires Nvidia compatibility and supply at enormous scale. The new order indicates that custom chips are expanding AWS’s capacity rather than displacing Nvidia in the near term. It also secures AWS access to Rubin-generation systems before those products become the industry’s standard deployment base.

## Why it matters

Two million additional GPUs materially expand the amount of frontier-model training and inference capacity scheduled to come online in 2027–28. The agreement also shows Nvidia converting its accelerator lead into a broader position spanning CPUs, networking, models and robotics. For Amazon, the unresolved question is whether demand and utilization will grow fast enough to justify the capital committed before the hardware arrives.

### Claude Cowork Adds an Isolated Built-In Browser

- Canonical: https://mmlong818.github.io/ai-pulse/articles/claude-cowork-built-in-browser.html
- Chinese: https://mmlong818.github.io/ai-pulse/zh/articles/claude-cowork-built-in-browser.html
- Source timestamp: 2026-08-26T23:26:00.000Z
- Site timestamp: 2026-08-27T11:00:03.973Z
- Tags: Agents, Safety

Anthropic is giving its desktop work agent a separate browser that can navigate sites and complete forms without controlling personal tabs.

## A browser dedicated to the agent

Anthropic has added a built-in browser to Claude Cowork, enabling its desktop agent to navigate websites, read pages, click controls, type and complete forms from a side panel. The feature is rolling out during the week to Pro, Max and Team subscribers on macOS, Windows and Linux beta. Enterprise administrators can enable it for their organizations immediately.

Unlike Claude in Chrome, the new browser is separated from the user’s everyday browser, tabs, bookmarks and saved passwords. Users may transfer selected logins from Chrome, Edge or Firefox on macOS, or from Firefox on Windows and Linux. Anthropic excludes banking, email and single-sign-on credentials from automatic transfer unless users explicitly choose otherwise. Logins established inside the dedicated browser can persist between Cowork sessions.

Claude in Chrome remains available and stays the default for existing extension users. Anthropic positions that extension for tasks involving an already-open page or active personal session, while the built-in browser is intended for delegated work such as gathering information, downloading invoices or operating a vendor portal. Tasks can also be directed from Claude’s web or mobile interfaces while the desktop application remains online.

## A different security boundary

The separation reduces the amount of personal browser state exposed by default, but it does not remove the central security problem of browser agents. Malicious instructions embedded in webpages can attempt to redirect an agent or induce unauthorized actions. Anthropic says the new browser uses the same action checks and prompt-injection defenses as Claude in Chrome, while acknowledging that those controls cannot eliminate the risk.

## Why it matters

A built-in browser turns Cowork into a more self-contained general-purpose agent: websites without connectors or APIs become actionable interfaces. The dedicated environment also gives Anthropic a clearer boundary for permissions and credentials than taking control of a user’s active browser. Adoption will depend on whether that isolation remains understandable when users begin importing logins and delegating consequential transactions.

### Google Launches Gemini 3.5 Transcribe in Preview

- Canonical: https://mmlong818.github.io/ai-pulse/articles/gemini-transcribe-speech-model.html
- Chinese: https://mmlong818.github.io/ai-pulse/zh/articles/gemini-transcribe-speech-model.html
- Source timestamp: 2026-08-26T17:01:00.000Z
- Site timestamp: 2026-08-26T23:00:03.019Z
- Tags: Models, Agents

Google’s new speech model handles live multilingual audio, cleans disfluencies and powers voice-driven workflows in products such as Gemini for macOS.

## Two models for live and recorded speech

Google introduced Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, a speech-to-text model offered in separate preview variants for real-time streaming and prerecorded audio. Developers can access it through the Gemini API and Google AI Studio, while Google is also using the technology in products including Gboard’s Rambler feature on Android and the Gemini app for macOS.

The prerecorded-audio model supports more than 85 languages, a 96,000-token input window and speaker attribution with timestamps for up to three speakers. Google reports word error rates of 5.04% on a selected group of FLEURS languages in non-streaming evaluation and 5.50% in streaming mode. Those results are Google’s own benchmark measurements and do not establish performance across every accent, acoustic setting or domain vocabulary.

## Transcription becomes an interface

The model is designed to produce usable prose rather than a strictly literal transcript. It can remove filler words, add punctuation and formatting, interpret spoken corrections, and improve recognition of phone numbers, postal codes and order identifiers. It also detects language changes during a conversation.

In the Gemini app for macOS, Google combines transcription with other Gemini models so spoken commands can initiate tasks such as image generation, information lookup, document summarization and file analysis. Google describes this product experience as function calling, but the current Gemini API documentation marks function calling as unsupported by the Transcribe endpoint itself. Developers therefore should not treat tool use as a native capability of either transcription API.

This product-level integration still turns transcription into an input layer for agents: a user can dictate, revise wording verbally and initiate a task without switching interfaces. The same flexibility raises accuracy and governance questions because removing disfluencies or interpreting intent can alter the evidentiary value of a transcript.

## Why it matters

Speech recognition is becoming infrastructure for agentic systems rather than a standalone conversion utility. Google can distribute this model across consumer software, enterprise tools and developer APIs, giving it unusually broad reach at launch. Its handling of alphanumeric strings addresses a persistent weakness in voice interfaces, while integrations such as Gemini for macOS connect speech to actions. Buyers will still need to distinguish polished dictation from faithful transcription—especially in medical, legal and compliance settings where an omitted hesitation or normalized phrase may carry meaning.

Chinese title: 谷歌推出Gemini 3.5 Transcribe语音转写模型
Chinese summary: 谷歌新模型支持实时多语种音频、自动清理口头停顿，并在Gemini macOS版等产品中为语音驱动的任务流程提供输入能力。
